title: Mission Statement, Legal Standing, & Core Values
content:
The San Andreas Department of Transportation (SADOT) is established as a cabinet-level civilian administrative agency of the state government. SADOT operates under direct regulatory mandates to oversee infrastructure maintenance, coordinate traffic safety initiatives, and deploy unified incident management across all state routes, freeways, and municipal secondary roadways.

Legal Limitation Directive SADOT is strictly a civilian government infrastructure and public safety agency, not a law enforcement organization. Under state civil code, personnel possess zero peace officer authority. Physical arrests, criminal investigations, vehicle pursuits, and moving traffic stops are strictly prohibited.
1.2 Comprehensive Mission Objective
Roadway Safety Preservation Actively identifying, staging against, and neutralizing physical infrastructure failures, debris fields, and hazardous road conditions.
Rapid Hazard Response Deploying advanced safety assets to mitigate blockages caused by mechanical failures, multi-car collisions, or adverse weather events.
Emergency Services Support Serving as a primary traffic support asset for Law Enforcement and Fire/EMS by establishing protective safety corridors and defensive blocking footprints.
Professional Traffic Control Executing precise structural lane closures, temporary detours, and manual flagging operations to isolate work zones and incident scenes.
Public Trust & Transparency Delivering high-fidelity, efficient public service that enhances the roleplay environment without dominating active scenes.
1.3 Core Values & Professional Tenets
Professionalism Public face of state government. Conduct all interactions and radio comms with calm, analytical discipline. Note: No pets or animals may be possessed by an operator on shift.
Safety Preservation of human life supersedes equipment recovery or clearance speed. Right to pause operations if a scene poses unmitigated life-safety hazards.
Realism Mirror authentic FHWA standards. Respect physical tool weights, deployment timelines, and geometric spacing. Instantaneous menu-built scene generation is barred.
Teamwork & Integrity Unified logistical front interfacing cleanly with emergency perimeters. Transparent, honest logging of all field actions and telemetry tracking.
1.4 Purpose & Dynamic Scope of the SOP Manual

Adherence to this manual is a mandatory condition of active employment; unauthorized deviation results in progressive disciplinary strikes or termination. Classified as a living framework, the text receives administrative revisions as vehicle codes and server mechanics update.

title: Departmental Structure & Chain of Command
content:
To maintain absolute operational safety, eliminate tracking confusion during high-stress roadway closures, and guarantee a unified logistical presence alongside emergency services, SADOT operates under a rigid, vertical Chain of Command (CoC) governing both administrative functions and tactical field deployments.

2.1 Protocol of Organizational Order

On-scene authority flows directly through established tiers. All personnel must route communications, field reports, and grievances through their immediate on-duty supervisor, except during life-safety overrides.

2.4 Communication Scaling & Escalation

Step 1: Supervisor → Step 2: Manager → Step 3: Executive Command. Chain-skipping introduces administrative friction and triggers strike logs.

2.2 & 2.3 Master Leadership & Field Rank Matrix
Command Staff
Transportation Commissioner Department executive; oversees agency policy, command appointments, and state logistics.
DOT-001
Deputy Transportation Commissioner Second-in-command; manages administrative workflows, disciplinary actions, and division heads.
DOT-002
Chief of Operations Oversees daily field deployments, major roadway closures, and fleet maintenance standards.
DOT-003
Supervisory Staff
Manager Senior district supervisor; conducts operational audits, MFO reviews, and onboarding sign-offs.
DOT-004
Supervisor Active tactical scene commanders; oversees lane shutdowns, mutual-aid calls, and field units.
DOT-005 – DOT-007
Field Operators
Senior Operator Lead field technician; certified for heavy wreckers, rotators, and complex highway tapers.
DOT-100 Series
Operator II Experienced operator; handles flatbed tows, winching, HazMat cleanup, and traffic routing.
DOT-200 Series
Operator I Full field operator; conducts routine road repairs, pothole patching, and basic scene setups.
DOT-300 Series
Probationary Operators
Cadet (Probationary Operator) Trainee in evaluation; restricted to Class I utility trucks under direct supervisor oversight.
DOT-400 Series
2.5 Emergency Scene Exemption & Immediate Tactical Overrides

The single definitive exception to the vertical CoC occurs during active field emergencies where strict adherence to communication scaling threatens human life safety:

Secondary Collision Risk Approaching motorist violating closed perimeter or secondary crash inside corridor.
Imminent Threat to Teams Police/Fire/EMS facing unmitigated structural hazards, flash fire, or environmental collapse.
Criminal Scene Escalation Civilian interaction turning into active criminal threat or armed assault with no supervisor present.

title: Recruitment, Onboarding, & Probationary Period
content:
All prospective applicants must satisfy strict entry-level criteria before receiving an appointment as a Probationary Operator. The department enforces dual-layered screening, rigorous technical certifications, and mandatory practical milestones to ensure operational readiness.

3.1 Core Employment Prerequisites & Background Screening
Licensing Mandate Valid, unexpired state driver’s license free of severe traffic warrants or active operational suspensions.
Background Check Successful clearance of baseline background checks confirming civil eligibility and identity.
Network Status Active rank of Probationary Civilian or higher within the primary network structure.
Disciplinary Window Clean record required. Active internal disciplinary actions or flags issued within the past rolling 30 days strictly disqualify entry.
3.2 The Probationary Operator (Cadet) Framework

Newly appointed personnel enter as Probationary Operators (Cadets) under direct supervisory oversight to evaluate technical viability, safety compliance, and professional standards.

Temporal Boundaries Standard Probationary Period spans seven (7) to fourteen (14) continuous calendar days.
Instructional Environment Cadets are restricted from independent operations and must execute all assignments under line-of-sight oversight of a certified field mentor or Supervisor.
3.3 Mandatory Technical Certifications & Practical Evaluations

Transitioning to full Operator status requires passing four mandatory practical milestone evaluations scored by a Supervisor or Manager:

A. Ride-Along Evaluation Analyzes live driving habits, adherence to speed thresholds, defensive driving protocols, navigation accuracy, and safe arrival positioning.
B. Traffic Stop Scene Training Verifies ability to apply protective positioning behind stationary emergency units and establish physical shadow areas shielding high-risk spaces.
C. Lane Closure Setup Assessment Evaluates geometric traffic-calming layouts, high-visibility cone placement, and arrow board/VMS configuration under active conditions.
D. Radio Communication Test Demonstrates plain-language/code transmission syntax, professional verbal tone, and instantaneous logging of status signals and callsigns.
3.4 Administrative Compliance & Roster Removal Triggers
The 14-Day Hard Cutoff All core technical evaluations, ride-alongs, and practical communication milestones must be fully completed and logged within the maximum 14-day window from initial appointment.
Roster Removal Mandate Failure to clear all four practical assessments within 14 days results in prompt administrative roster removal, stripping vehicle spawn permissions and requiring formal reapplication.

title: Primary Duties & Operational Limitations
content:
The San Andreas Department of Transportation is structurally restricted to the execution of public works, civil incident mitigation, and infrastructure preservation tasks. Personnel must strictly observe operational boundaries; crossing into law enforcement roles, vigilante traffic policing, or abandoning assigned work will result in immediate termination.

Critical Jurisdictional Prohibition Matrix SADOT personnel absolutely do not possess police or peace officer authorizations. The following actions are strictly forbidden:
  1. Absolute Arrest Prohibition: No detaining or arresting of citizens.
  2. Investigative Restriction: No criminal investigations or searches.
  3. Kinetic Pursuit Ban: No active pursuing of fleeing suspect vehicles.
  4. Interdiction Ban: No traffic stops on moving civilian motorists.
4.1 Authorized Field Actions & Tactical Directives
A. Traffic Control Operations Lane closures, taper geometries, detour coordination, manual flagger operations, and scene perimeter management with physical barriers and delineators.
B. Motorist Roadside Assistance Low-speed vehicle push-offs, pneumatic tire wheel exchanges, and emergency fuel replenishment (1–2 gallons) to enable motorist self-evacuation.
C. Macro-Scale Major Incidents Tier-1 support for Law Enforcement and Fire/EMS including total roadway shutdowns, strategic traffic diversions, hazardous debris extraction, and mobile light tower illumination.
4.2 Absolute Statutory & Legal Limitations
A. Arrest & Detainment Prohibition Zero authority to deprive individual liberty. No handcuffs, zip-ties, or verbal commands to hold suspects. Document confessions via surveillance and request LEO intervention.
B. Investigation Exclusion Crime scene processing and evidence collection belong exclusively to LEO. Prohibited from searching vehicle interiors or property; secure perimeter and await LEO command.
C. Emergency Pursuits Ban Strictly barred from engaging in pursuits or interdicting fleeing vehicles, using emergency lights to shadow targets, or blocking paths. Transmit tracking data to Dispatch.
D. Moving Traffic Interdiction Ban Warning lights and sirens are for static scene preservation only. Conducting unauthorized traffic stops triggers automatic internal review, roster termination, and potential server blacklist flags.
Authorized Field Duties
  • Freeway, highway, and local road surface maintenance.
  • Live traffic lane closures, cone tapers, and detour routing.
  • Disabled vehicle recovery, winching, and transport.
  • Debris clearance, fallen tree removal, and downed wire isolation.
  • Assisting emergency services with scene protection and outer perimeters.
Strict Operational Prohibitions
  • Conducting traffic stops, issuing citations, or detaining civilians.
  • Entering active felony stops, gunfire zones, or un-cleared crime scenes.
  • Engaging in vehicle pursuits or executing PIT maneuvers in state units.
  • Carrying lethal firearms or unapproved tactical equipment while on duty.
  • Operating state apparatus off-duty for personal recreation or transport.

title: Field Scene Protocols & Traffic Management Guide
content:
The first sixty seconds of arrival at an active incident zone dictate the long-term safety profile of the scene. Every field scene must be established using standardized mathematical geometry, defensive staging methodologies, and strict coordination with Law Enforcement Command.

5.1 Incident Arrival & Tactical Staging Workflows
Radio Status Notification State call sign and formally announce arrival on operational net using clean phrasing (e.g., “DOT-12 is 10-23 at the Senora Fwy incident.”).
Safe Staging Distance Strictly prohibit pulling units directly into active incident zones or LEO perimeters. Stage field assets 25 to 50 feet back from the primary incident pocket or along the shoulder.
Buffer & Pre-Exit Assessment Maintain defensive buffers until declared Code 4 by LEO or Supervisor. Conduct visual assessments of sightlines, blind crests, and traffic speeds from inside the cabin.
5.2 Interaction with Law Enforcement & Scene Command Transfer
Absolute LEO Authority On scenes with active emergency responders, law enforcement holds complete Scene Commander authority. Arriving SADOT units must remain near vehicles and await explicit command instructions.
Formal Roadway Command Transfer Once LEO formally releases the scene, the senior on-scene SADOT unit assumes absolute command of local traffic management and equipment allocations until all debris and assets are cleared.
5.3 Geometric Cone Spacing & Tapering Guidelines
City & Municipal Roads Space channelizing cones at strict 5 to 10 feet intervals for low-speed urban turns and compact lane transitions.
Highways & Expressways Space channelizing cones at 10 to 20 feet intervals to accommodate high-velocity approaching traffic and extended braking distances.
Major Arterial Closures Utilize extended gradual tapers stretching back a minimum of 50 to 100 feet from the hazard zone boundary.
🔍 Inspect Freeway Taper Diagram (FIG 5.1)
FIG 5.1: High-Speed Corridor Taper & Attenuator Placement Speed Formula Standard
Taper Distance Formula (Speeds ≥ 45 MPH)

L = W × S

Where L is Taper Length, W is Lane Width (12 ft), and S is Speed Limit (MPH).

12 ft × 65 MPH = 780 ft (~240m / ~20-25 car lengths in-game)
Attenuator / Shadow Vehicle Staging

Station the barrier truck 100 feet prior to the work zone with amber directional chevrons engaged. Front wheels must be turned towards the shoulder/guardrail away from working personnel.

title: Radio Communication & Protocol
content:
SADOT operates on dedicated municipal dispatch frequencies monitored by supervisors and inter-agency dispatchers. Radio traffic must remain strictly operational, professional, and formatted according to standardized 10-code brevity.

10-4 Acknowledged

Confirms that the operator has fully received, processed, and understood the parameters of the previous transmission.

10-6 Busy

Informs the dispatch controller and surrounding units that the operator is temporarily occupied with an intensive field task and cannot immediately accept secondary dispatches or respond to voice queries.

10-7 Unavailable / Out-of-Service

Indicates that the unit is terminating its active shift, logging out of the tracking network, and is completely unavailable for field assignments.

10-8 Available / In-Service

Signals that the unit is fully operational, fueled, actively on patrol, and open to receive immediate incident dispatches.

10-9 Repeat

Requests the immediate retransmission of the previous statement due to poor signal quality, heavy static, or overlapping audio feeds.

10-20 Location

Initiates a positional query or provides a precise tracking update, which must include the nearest map postal code, primary thoroughfare name, and intersecting crossroads.

10-23 On Scene

Confirms that the response unit has arrived at the incident coordinates and is actively configuring its defensive block and staging perimeter.

10-33 Clear

Indicates that all primary recovery, debris extraction, and traffic management tasks are finalized, foot equipment is safely packed away, and the unit is departing the coordinates.

En Route Status Protocol Communicates that the unit has cleared its staging yard or patrol sector and is actively traversing toward a specific dispatched landmark.
EN ROUTE

title: Fleet Vehicle Code, Classification, & Telemetry
content:
To establish an unmistakable government presence and project absolute uniform authority on the highways of San Andreas, the Department of Transportation enforces a rigid standardization policy across 100 percent of its active fleet vehicles. Arbitrary aesthetic modifications, custom liveries, non-vetted paint profiles, or unauthorized parts swaps are strictly prohibited and classified as equipment non-compliance violations.

7.1 Branding, Paint, and Registration Standards
The Fleet Paint Policy:

Every active vehicle placed into service must utilize a solid, uniform finish of Orange (Color Code 24, Metallic) across all primary and secondary body panels. No custom decals, corporate wrap variants, or accent liveries are permitted on state-owned equipment.

State Registration Mandate:

Prior to clearing any regional depot gate line, the operator must verify that the vehicle is running a standardized government license plate configured to read SA DOT verbatim. Civilian plates or outdated identifiers result in immediate red-tag grounding.

Window Tint Restrictions:

To maintain operator visibility and satisfy highway safety guidelines, window film application is limited strictly to stock glass or light smoke configurations. Dark tint or limousine-grade black-out applications are entirely banned.

Wheel and Rim Compliance:

Vehicle rims must be set strictly to standard industrial, heavy-duty, or commercial configurations corresponding directly to manufacturing class. Sports wheels, custom street rims, colored accents, or off-road modifications on urban units are heavily penalized.

7.2 Master Vehicle Allocation & Rank Tier Matrix Spawn & Extra Configuration Mandate

Operating a fleet unit above your verified rank or technical certification tier without express written Command Staff authorization or emergency override is strictly prohibited. Operators must verify vMenu extra toggles prior to dispatch.

A. Entry and Basic Operational Tier (Patrols, Hazard Tracking & Motorist Assist)
Chevy Tahoe (civtahoe) — Cadet+ Extras: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 11, 12
Dodge Ram 3500 HD (civramdot1) — Operator I+ Extras: 10, 11, 12
Ford F550 Rollback Cab 1.5 (f550rollback1) — Operator I+ Extras: 1, 2, 3
B. Advanced Field Tiers (Intermediate Scenes, Lane Closures & Recovery)
Ford F150 (civf150) — Operator II+ (Mandatory Livery Required) Extras: 1, 2, 9, 10, 11, 12
Dodge Ram 5500 HD Rollback (ramrollback) — Operator II+ Extras: 5
Ford F550 Rollback (f550rollback2) — Senior Operator+ Extras: 1, 4, 9, 11
Ford F550 Arrow Board Utility (civf550dot) — Senior Operator+ Extras: 2, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11
Dodge Ram 5500 HD Arrow Board Utility (civramdot2) — Senior Operator+ Extras: 2, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11
C. Logistics, Heavy Duty, and Supervisory Fleet Cross-Authorization Clause

Supervisor+ exclusive. Ranks below Supervisor (Operator I, II, Senior) are strictly barred from spawning or operating these assets unless possessing an active, verified Heavy Duty (HVY) Certification on profile.

Dodge Durango (civdurango) — Supervisor+ Extras: 1, 6
Kenworth Wrecker (kenworthwrecker) — Supervisor+ / HVY Cert Extras: 1, 2, 3, 5, 10
International Navistar Rollback (navistarrollback) — Supervisor+ / HVY Cert Extras: N/A
Kenworth W900 Heavy Semi-Tractor (w900) — Supervisor+ / HVY Cert All Active EXCEPT Extra 10
D. Specialized Departmental Towing Trailers (Physics Hitching Protocol)
Enclosed Car Trailer (cartrailer1) — All ranks w/ Trailer Cert Extras: 4, 5, 6
Tritoon Boat Trailer (ptrailer) — All ranks w/ Trailer Cert Extras: N/A
Lowboy Heavy Transport Trailer (trlowboy) — Supervisor+ / HVY Cert Hitch: Extra 1 ON

Loading Sequence: Decouple, toggle Extra 1 to OFF, and toggle Extra 3 to ON to drop ramps flush to pavement. Verify Fenders 1 (Option 2) and Oversize Load 1 (Option 2) active prior to hauling.

7.3 Fleet Telemetry, Surveillance, & Asset Tracking Matrix
A. Multi-Angle Dashcam Integration (Automatic Ignition Initialization)

Surveillance arrays initialize automatically upon engine ignition. Camera feeds are hard-locked across three angles and cannot be deactivated:

  • Front-Facing Lens: Wide-angle view of oncoming traffic flow, work zone perimeters, and advance cone tapers.
  • Rear-Facing Lens: Dedicated surveillance of the rear utility bed, towing apparatus, winch lines, and trailing loads.
  • Interior Cockpit Lens: Documents driver control inputs, radio communications, and in-cab safety compliance.
B. Real-Time LoJack Geo-Tracking Telemetry

Every chassis contains a welded LoJack transmitter linking coordinates, velocities, and engine telemetry directly to CAD. Disconnecting, masking, or tampering with tracking hardware constitutes gross negligence subject to immediate suspension or termination. Data is mirrored locally in a hardened console frame and synced via redundant cellular bands to the secure SADOT Cloud Server repository.

C. Evidence Archiving & Incident Review Access

All telemetry metrics and footage are stored on a rolling thirty (30) day retention hold under exclusive Command Staff custody. Stored records stand as definitive legal evidence during motorist disputes, civil injury claims, or inter-agency inquiries.

title: Equipment Operational Matrix & Trailer Guidelines
content:
Field towing, rollback flatbed winching, boom recovery, and multi-asset transport require absolute structural awareness, correct mechanical interface inputs, and precise script controls to ensure zero equipment failure and operator survival.

8.1 Rollback Deployment & Recovery Protocols f550rollback1 / silveradorollback / ramrollback

To prevent mechanical tipping or hydraulic frame distortion, operators must ensure the chassis is parked on level ground before extending the bed. Reverse until the rear apron is roughly 10 to 15 feet from the casualty's bumper, shift into park, and set the emergency air brake.

Hydraulic Bed Slider Controls
[Down Arrow] : Lower & slide bed back flush to road
[Up Arrow] : Raise & slide bed forward to travel lock
Winch & Securement Controls
[Right Arrow] : Free-spool/unwind winch cable
[Left Arrow] : Winch vehicle up onto platform
[G] : Detach cable hook (when bed fully up)
[E] : Engage wheel tie-down straps / chains
8.2 Boom & Wrecker Operations kenworthwrecker
Critical Life-Safety Mandate Under no circumstances should any boom apparatus, hydraulic hook, or winch line be actuated, tensioned, or moved while a civilian or officer remains inside the cabin of the target vehicle. The cabin must be confirmed 100% clear.
Keyboard Control Map
[Left Shift] : Hydraulics Raise main boom
[Left Ctrl] : Hydraulics Lower main boom
[H] : Drop / Release wheel-lift or hook array
Controller Control Map
[Left Stick Up] : Hydraulics Raise main boom
[Left Stick Down] : Hydraulics Lower main boom
[D-Pad Right] : Drop / Release wheel-lift or hook array
8.3 Advanced Cargo Securing (/attach System) Mandatory for Trailers & HVY Loads

When securing irregular cargo, multiple collision wrecks, or heavy equipment onto beds, execute /attach in chat. Press [Enter] while aiming at the transport bed, then press [Enter] on the cargo item to link entities.

[Numpad 8 / 5] : Shift Forward / Backward
[Numpad 4 / 6] : Shift Left / Right
[Page Up / Down] : Elevate Up / Down
[Numpad 7 / 9] : Yaw Rotation (Left / Right)
[Insert / Delete] : Pitch Rotation (Angle to ramp)
[Numpad Enter] : Lock Position to Flatbed
Modifiers: Hold [Shift] for rapid translation | Hold [Ctrl] for fine adjustments. Execute /detach at delivery.
8.4 Specialized Trailer Logistics & Deployment Hitch: [J] | Detach: [H] or [D-Pad Right Hold]
Lowboy Heavy Transporter (trlowboy) Supervisor+ / HVY Cert

Unhitch truck from trailer neck. Press [F] at side neck controls. Toggle Extra 1 OFF and Extra 3 ON in vMenu to uncouple safety blocks and drop ramps flush to pavement. Drive equipment on and secure via /attach. Re-toggle Extra 3 OFF and Extra 1 ON to raise the neck before re-hitching via [J]. Verify Fenders 1 (Opt 2) & Oversize Load 1 (Opt 2) active.

Enclosed Car Trailer (cartrailer1) Trailer Cert

Approach rear tailgate structure and press [E] to deploy ramps. Stage vehicles inside the enclosed bay, then press [G] to execute Mass-Attach. At destination, lower tail gate and press [H] to trigger Mass-Detach before driving vehicles off.

Tritoon Boat Trailer (ptrailer) Trailer Cert

Back trailer down ramp until bunks submerge below waterline. Use /attach to winch vessel hull snug against bow stop. Scale Restriction: Vessels exceeding structural trailer bunks (luxury yachts, multi-deck cruisers, tugboats) are barred from recovery—deny service and request offshore salvage.

title: Use of Force & Defensive Disengagement Policy
content:
SADOT personnel are civil state maintenance professionals, not peace officers. Department members hold zero authority to enforce laws, detain suspects, or engage hostile threats. Self-preservation and defensive tactical retreat are mandatory.

9.1 Non-Combatant Status and Strict Limitations of Force

The San Andreas Department of Transportation is a civilian administrative public works agency, not a kinetic tactical group or law enforcement body. Consequently, all department personnel operate under a strict non-combatant designation.

Absolute Force Prohibition Except in extreme, un-mitigative environments where an operator faces an immediate threat of death or serious bodily harm, personnel are strictly prohibited from engaging in physical violence, initiating physical altercations, or participating in structural combat.
Statutory Weaponry Restrictions Operators possess no statutory legal authority to brandish, deploy, or discharge lethal firearms while executing official department duties. The deployment of lethal force is entirely outside the operational scope of the department.
Imminent Harm Threshold Physical force of any description may only be utilized as an absolute last resort, strictly for self-preservation and defensive block manipulation, when life or serious bodily injury is completely imminent and the situation is entirely unavoidable.
9.2 Authorized Defensive Hardware & Less-Lethal Equipment Strictly Non-Lethal / Self-Defense Only

To maintain personal security during remote highway maintenance runs or night-shift debris clearings, personnel are granted restricted authorization to possess defensive hardware on their utility belts.

Zero-Tolerance Firearms Ban Firearms are strictly prohibited from being used and carried by any employee in any capacity. Pepper spray and batons are authorized exclusively as less-than-lethal tools to carry for self-defense against wild animals or immediate personal assault.

Defensive tools must remain completely concealed or securely holstered within utility pouches during routine operations. Brandishing department-issued tools to intimidate competing logistics workers, threaten civilians, or escalate minor parking verbal altercations is a critical violation that triggers immediate disciplinary action.

9.3 Critical Life-Safety Evacuation Mandate Mandatory Tactical Retreat Protocol

The Department of Transportation places the personal survival and life safety of its ground technicians completely above the preservation of state property, fleet vehicles, or infrastructure assets. Operators are mandated to disengage the moment a scene encounters criminal threats, armed suspects, weapons discharges, or severe structural violence.

STEP 1 CEASE OPERATIONS Terminate all winching, paving, and maintenance workflows instantly.
STEP 2 ABANDON HARDWARE Drop all physical hand tools, traffic cones, barriers, and gear on scene.
STEP 3 TACTICAL RETREAT Evacuate the sector immediately via the safest available corridor.
STEP 4 PRESERVE LIFE Leave fleet trucks behind if keys are inaccessible; prioritize human life.

Relocation & Escalation: Retreat to secure coordinates outside the hot zone (e.g., nearest LEO precinct or regional yard). Instantly broadcast a priority emergency ping or call law enforcement dispatch to request immediate armed intervention.

Asset Recovery Restraints: Personnel are strictly prohibited from re-entering the evacuated zone to retrieve abandoned state vehicles, tools, or trailers. Equipment remains abandoned until law enforcement command officially declares the entire sector Code 4 and issues a direct security escort back to the coordinates.

9.4 Post-Incident Reporting & Administrative Telemetry Holds

Any event triggering a defensive disengagement, less-lethal deployment, or unmitigated retreat is classified as a critical incident.

Supervisor Briefing Window The evacuated operator must provide a direct voice briefing to an active on-duty Supervisor or Manager within thirty (30) minutes of clearing the hazard zone.
Automated Video Protection Lock Upon receiving a critical incident report, Command Staff execute a mandatory data lock on SADOT Cloud Servers, hard-locking multi-angle dashcams and LoJack telemetry logs against rolling recycling to preserve evidence.

title: Progressive Disciplinary Action Framework (Strike System)
content:
As an administrative civil service agency, SADOT enforces strict operational compliance. The Command Staff utilizes a formalized Progressive Disciplinary Action Framework structured around a three-tier strike directive and immediate termination offenses.

10.2 Progressive Penalty Structure (The Strike System)
Strike 1 Verbal Counseling

Issued for initial technical errors, minor procedural oversights, or low-risk omissions. Involves a formal re-education session with a Supervisor and internal personnel logging.

Record Duration: 30 Days
Strike 2 Written Warning & Suspension

Triggered by secondary infractions or safety protocol violations. Involves a formal written reprimand, 1-3 day operational field suspension, and promotional lockout.

Sanction: 1–3 Day Suspension
Strike 3 Command Review Board

Triggered by un-remedied third accumulations or gross technical negligence. Results in vehicle key suspension and Command Board evaluation leading to demotion or termination.

Sanction: Demotion or Termination
10.3 Comprehensive Classification of Infractions
A. Minor Procedural Infractions (Strike 1 Path)

Returning fleet units with less than 1/4 fuel, improper compound parking (nose-out rule), minor radio etiquette/format slips, and clearing depot without complete service kits (flares, vests).

B. Major Non-Compliance Infractions (Strike 2 Path)

Misuse of amber strobes during non-emergency transit or off-duty travel, failing to secure LEO signatures on tracking forms, operating out of uniform/high-vis gear, and failing to report vehicle damage or minor yard/field accidents.

C. Critical Misconduct Infractions (Strike 3 / Board Review Path)

Spawning specialized vehicle classes above verified rank/tier without authorization, unprofessional language or arguments with dispatch, and wrecker life-safety negligence (operating winch/boom while a civilian remains inside target vehicle cabin).

10.4 Immediate Termination Offenses (Bypasses Progressive Discipline)
Fail RP & Server Rules Violating baseline server regulations or executing Fail RP while signed into active department duty.
Malicious Abuse of Power Exploiting administrative permissions or towing scripts to maliciously disrupt civilian roleplay configurations.
Personal Asset Exploitation Utilizing department fleet vehicles, arrow trucks, or light arrays for personal off-duty civilian scenarios.
Inter-Departmental Hostility Displaying gross disrespect, insubordination, or verbal hostility toward allied emergency departments (LEO/EMS).
10.5 Accumulation Rules, Roster Holds, and Promotion Lockouts
The 30-Day Disciplinary Window Any formal strike mark, written warning, or verbal counseling entry remains live and active on a profile for a continuous duration of thirty (30) days from the formal adjudication date.
Promotion & Roster Lockouts Active strikes completely disqualify operators from rank advancements or specialized certification checkouts regardless of activity hours. 3 active strikes within 90 days triggers permanent database removal and CAD revocation.

title: Promotion & Career Advancement Tiers
content:
Advancement within the department is strictly volume-driven, merit-based, and governed by transparent evaluation parameters. The department explicitly rejects subjective baselines or hourly time-clock structures, replacing them with a framework evaluating technical proficiency, roleplay quality, professional decorum, scene staging geometry, and unblemished disciplinary profiles.

11.1 & 11.2 The Five Core Parameters of Evaluation
[Activity Metrics] + [RP Quality] + [Professionalism] + [Scene Control] + [No Active Strikes] = Promotion Eligible
A. Activity Metrics

Cadet–Operator II fulfill monthly Flag Assist quotas. Senior+ fulfill vehicle transport quotas. Minimum 3 operational hours per month required.

B. Roleplay Quality

Procedural authenticity, physical weight of equipment handling, avoiding menu-spawning shortcuts, and building immersive accident scenes.

C. Professionalism

Flawless radio telephony ("From-To" syntax), measured tone, and calm civilian de-escalation mastery during high-stress disputes.

D. Scene Control

FHWA geometry compliance, defensive vehicle angling for safety corridors, speed-compliant cone tapers, and dynamic traffic routing.

E. Disciplinary Clearance (30-Day Reset)

An unblemished profile free of active flags or reprimands. A single strike mark or warning immediately freezes advancement eligibility for 30 consecutive calendar days.

11.3 Detailed Eligibility Requirements by Advancement Tier
Cadet (Probationary) → Operator I 7 to 14 days under supervisory monitoring; successful completion of Ride-Along, Traffic Stop Scene, Lane Closure Setup, and Radio Comms evaluations; zero active strike logs.
Operator I → Operator II Minimum 21 active calendar days in placement; maintenance of Support Pathway standing with a minimum of 10 verified Flag Assists per month; formal written supervisory recommendation.
Operator II → Senior Operator Minimum 30 active calendar days; graduation to independent transport operations with a minimum log of 15 successful vehicle clearances or flatbed rollbacks; demonstrated multi-lane freeway diversion management.
11.4 Executive Command Board Appointments (Manager & Higher)

Progression to Supervisory or Management brackets shifts focus from tactical execution to administrative accountability. Candidates cannot solicit promotions; appointments require an unprompted written recommendation from an active Supervisor.

Comprehensive Audit Portfolios are audited across 100% of LoJack telemetry, dashcam recordings, shift logs, and historical disciplinary files.
Board Voting & Finality Requires majority executive vote (Chief of Operations & Transportation Commissioners). Rulings are final and binding; unsuccessful candidates face a mandatory 45-day reset window.

title: Inter-Agency Cooperation & Unified Incident Command
content:
The San Andreas Department of Transportation operates as a primary trusted civilian infrastructure and public safety asset alongside emergency services. To ensure maximum scene safety, efficient asset allocation, and rapid transit restoration, SADOT works in close conjunction with municipal police, the Sheriff's Office, and Fire/EMS departments.

12.2 The Unified Chain of Scene Command
Absolute LEO Jurisdiction On active scenes featuring emergency responders or traffic hazards, responding law enforcement officers maintain absolute, definitive Scene Commander authority.
Operational Restraint Personnel are prohibited from independently moving vehicles or altering perimeters without direct instructions from police authorities. Park defensively, remain with vehicles, and await tactical orders.
Police Line Exclusion Technicians must not step past cordoned police or forensic boundaries unless explicitly requested by the LEO Scene Commander to move debris or execute heavy winching.
12.3 Structural Roadway Command Transfer Protocols

Once emergency life-safety operations conclude, patient extractions are finalized, and law enforcement officers formally release an accident or impound scene, absolute tactical command of the coordinates is officially transferred to the SADOT crew.

SADOT Command Activation Senior on-scene SADOT unit instantly assumes absolute command of local traffic configurations, lane templates, cleanup operations, and vehicle management.
Scene Closure Mandate Arriving support units take direct orders from the senior technician managing the transfer until all hazards are cleared and the transit corridor is restored to standard traffic codes.
12.4 Specific Agency Interfacing Matrices
A. Law Enforcement Interfacing (Police & Sheriff)

Staging Alignment: Stage trucks 25 to 50 feet behind the outermost law enforcement vehicle, utilizing arrow boards to deflect civilian traffic away from the police contact pocket.

Impound & Evidence Escorts: Verify the initiating officer's unique identity metrics and secure an official signature before moving forensic/impounded hardware. Follow directly behind the primary LEO cruiser with synchronized amber strobes.

B. Fire & EMS Interfacing

Hazard Corridor Isolation: On scenes containing active fires or fluid spills, Fire Command holds absolute immediate command. SADOT units must establish multi-lane diversion zones well ahead of fire apparatus to prevent civilian interference.

Tactical Lighting Support: Position advanced arrow trucks or utility rigs to project clean, non-glare illumination onto night-time extrications or medical triage work zones without blinding oncoming motorists.

title: Activity, Logistical Standby, & Reporting Requirements
content:
Accountability ensures coverage across all state highways and county roads. Operators on duty must maintain accurate activity logs, adhere to standby positioning guidelines, and comply with monthly participation baselines and training mandates.

Shift Logging & Form Submission

Operators must log in at the start of their shift (10-8) and log out upon conclusion (10-42) using the official department portal. All work orders, scene setups, towing transports, and material usage must be submitted via the designated reporting forms before going off duty.

Logistical Standby Staging

When not assigned to an active work order or highway patrol circuit, units on standby must stage at designated department yards (Davis Maintenance Yard, Paleto Bay Depot, or Sandy Shores Facility). Staging in active civilian parking lots or blocking thoroughfares while idle is prohibited.

13.1 Standard Operational Activity Baselines

To maintain operational readiness, ensure adequate staffing across all functional shifts, and maximize state vehicle utility, SADOT enforces a mandatory minimum activity baseline evaluated on a continuous monthly cycle.

The Monthly Log Requirement All active roster personnel must log a minimum of three (3) operational hours per month directly recorded within the official departmental patrol log to maintain active employment standing.
Time Tracking Mechanism Active hours are tracked using telemetry links from vehicle terminals and verified against patrol log entries. Operators are individually responsible for documenting shift durations prior to going off duty.
Consequences of Non-Compliance Failure to meet the three-hour monthly minimum results in an immediate shift to inactive status, suspending vehicle authorization keys and restricting database access pending supervisory review.
13.2 Mandatory Training & Operational Workshop Requirements

The preservation of incident scenes and highway safety configurations requires continuous technical instruction and practical skill refinement through scheduled training protocols.

Attendance & Training Scope Attendance at scheduled training blocks, lane-closure workshops, or mock disaster drills is mandatory. Instruction audits vehicle stabilization, lowboy ramp physics, lighting compliance, and radio telephony.
Excusal Protocol & Penalties Absences require a formal, documented leave notice approved by a Supervisor prior to the event. Unexcused non-attendance results in inactive status and immediate suspension of vehicle authorization keys.
13.3 Leave of Absence (LOA) & Roster Protection Regulations

The department provides a structured administrative process for personnel who must temporarily step away from active service due to external commitments, protecting their roster placement and rank certifications.

Filing Requirements & Adjudication Holds longer than 7 consecutive calendar days require an LOA package detailing activation and return dates. Up to 14 days may be signed off by a Manager; extended holds exceeding 14 days require Command Staff review and Chief of Operations approval.
Exemption & Unapproved Inactivity Approved LOA completely exempts personnel from the 3-hour monthly minimum and securely locks rank/certification profiles. Unapproved inactivity exceeding a rolling 45-day window flags profiles as abandoned, resulting in permanent credential deactivation.

title: Realism, Immersion, & Roleplay Standards
content:
SADOT exists as a public safety utility engineered explicitly to enhance the overall roleplay environment. Personnel do not operate to dominate scene environments; instead, the department builds a high-fidelity layer of realism supporting allied emergency services and providing visual fidelity for passing motorists.

14.1 Philosophy of Scene Enhancement

Operators must balance tactical duties with a strict commitment to high-fidelity immersion, ensuring that state operations never disrupt or break the server's core roleplay boundaries.

14.2 Absolute Prohibition of Powergaming and Unrealistic Scene Generation
Weight of Equipment Roleplay the true physical weight, bulk, and mechanical handling constraints of all tools and safety assets.
Menu Generation Ban Instantaneous spawning or removal of assets via user interface menus while in the active view of other players is strictly prohibited. Use physical interactions.
Unrealistic Closures Avoid disproportionate defensive blocks or physics-defying barrier placements that seal off massive roadway sectors without supervisor direction.
14.3 Strict Prohibition of Metagaming within Department Logistics

Personnel must maintain clean administrative separation between out-of-character (OOC) communication platforms and in-character (IC) field actions.

Dispatch Validation Mandate Units may only respond to incidents if calls originate through official IC channels: active radio telephony (RTO), official CAD terminal pings, or direct in-person requests from law enforcement or civilian motorists. Un-marked text pings are prohibited.
14.4 Immersive Staging & Visual Delineation Standards
Authentic Work Zone Aesthetics Cones must form clean, straight lines matching standard tapering guides. Electronic message boards must display text corresponding directly to active hazards.
Immersive Civilian Interactions Roleplay technical execution during roadside assistance (e.g., checking lug nut torques or hydraulic pressures) to provide an authentic experience.

title: Traffic Lights, Signage, & Electronic Display Operations
content:
Traffic signals, stationary highway signage, and dynamic electronic message arrays represent critical control elements of state roadway infrastructure. SADOT crews maintain, repair, and deploy these assets to preserve structural traffic order and prevent secondary collisions.

15.1 Operational Scope & Deployment Criteria
A. Traffic Light Servicing Triggered by power failures, storm damage, knock-downs, or cabinet malfunctions. Restores active intersection regulation to eliminate immediate life-safety hazards.
B. Road Sign Repair & Knock-Downs Triggered by damaged or missing regulatory/warning signs. Critical regulatory signs (STOP/YIELD) require priority emergency response within two (2) hours of notification.
C. VMS & Arrow Board Deployment Used for long-term construction, freeway lane closures, or weather warnings to provide high-visibility advance warnings for braking and merging.
D. Temporary Closure Signage Activated during total road shutdowns or detours to direct civilian traffic safely around closed infrastructure without local gridlock.
15.2 Field Execution & Safety Protocols
Step 1: Pre-Deployment & Site Isolation Deploy utility warning tapers (civf550dot/civramdot2) and cones per Section 5.3. Isolate local breaker circuits at controller cabinets for Lockout / Tagout (LOTO) power safety.
Step 2: Traffic Light Maintenance & Signal Replacement Deploy temporary four-way STOP signs or flaggers if signals are disabled. Position bucket trucks with outriggers deployed on stable ground; secure tethered safety harnesses. Exchange signal heads, restore cabinet power, and cycle manual phase tests before clearing.
Step 3: Road Sign Repair & Post Installation Extract sheared anchor sleeves, drive new breakaway sleeves, and bolt reflective aluminum sign panels at standard height (7 ft urban / 5 ft rural from pavement to base).
Step 4: Variable Message Board (VMS) Setup Stage trailer 500–1,000 ft ahead of work zones, lower leveling jacks, unhitch if stationary, and raise solar mast. Program short 3-line FHWA abbreviations with flash rates allowing drivers to read messages twice at highway speeds.
15.3 Specialized Training & Practical Qualification Curriculum

Operators must complete the Traffic Control Infrastructure & Signage Module under direct supervision of a certified Manager or Supervisor.

Instructional Modules
  • T-1 (MUTCD Signage): Placement, retroreflectivity, and height/offset rules.
  • T-2 (Aerial Lift Safety): Outriggers, weight limits, manual descent, and fall protection.
  • T-3 (Signal Cabinets): Logic controllers, conflict monitors, and LOTO procedures.
Practical Field Evaluations
  • Eval 1: Emergency STOP & Detour setup anchored within 10 minutes of arrival.
  • Eval 2: Bucket truck positioning, harness tethering, and mock signal head swap.
  • Eval 3: VMS trailer leveling, mast elevation, and 1,000-ft visibility audit.

title: Roadwork & Road Maintenance
content:
State roadway networks suffer continuous wear and tear from heavy traffic volume, thermal expansion, severe weather events, and vehicular collisions. SADOT road maintenance crews are tasked with maintaining pavement integrity, clearing travel lanes, and repairing structural barriers to prevent vehicle accidents and preserve regional infrastructure.

16.1 Operational Scope & Deployment Criteria
A. Pothole Repair Triggered by spalling or rim-damaging potholes. Restores smoothness to prevent blowouts, rim damage, and sudden swerving.
B. Road Resurfacing Triggered by structural failure, rutting, or mill-and-overlay projects. Lays fresh surface layers across extended corridors to extend roadway lifespans.
C. Lane & Roadway Closures Required whenever personnel or machinery encroach upon live travel lanes, establishing a protected physical work corridor.
D. Debris Removal Clears shredded tires, dropped cargo, or fallen tree branches from live lanes and restores soft/hard shoulders for emergency stops.
E. Guardrail & Barrier Repair Repairs crushed W-beam rails or displaced Jersey barriers to prevent vehicles from crossing medians or embankments.
F. Roadway Inspections Routine patrols and post-storm audits to identify emerging road hazards, failing drainage, or missing signage early.
16.2 Field Execution & Safety Protocols
Step 1: Work Zone Setup & Mobile Shadow Protection Position arrow trucks (civf550dot/civramdot2) 250–500 ft upstream with cone tapers per Section 5.3. Place secondary shadow trucks 50 ft upstream of workers on live lanes.
Step 2: Pothole & Localized Pavement Repair Workflow Clear cavity debris, apply asphalt emulsion tack coat, and fill with hot/cold-mix asphalt in 2-inch lifts. Compact firmly using a vibratory compactor until patch sits 1/4 inch above surrounding grade.
Step 3: High-Speed Highway Debris Clearance Deploy a two-truck rolling block. Secondary technician exits lead truck, retrieves debris into utility bed, and re-enters cabin within 30 seconds.
Step 4: Guardrail Repair & Realignment Unbolt damaged W-beam panels, extract sheared posts, drive new galvanized I-beam posts, and mount replacement rails with splices overlapping traffic flow. Drag shifted Jersey barriers using kenworthwrecker with HVY Certification.
Step 5: Roadway Inspection Patrols Operate marked patrol units (civtahoe/civf250) at reduced speeds on shoulders with amber strobes active. Log precise postal codes and hazard severity into onboard terminals.
16.3 Specialized Training & Practical Qualification Curriculum

Personnel performing road maintenance must complete the Roadway Operations & Infrastructure Maintenance Module supervised by a Manager or Supervisor.

Instructional Modules
  • Module R-1: Pavement repair mechanics, compaction physics, and joint sealing.
  • Module R-2: Crash attenuation, W-beam guardrails, and Jersey barrier protocols.
  • Module R-3: Mobile debris extraction and rolling block tactical coordination.
Practical Field Evaluations
  • Eval 1: Flush pothole patching completed within 15 minutes (±1/8 inch tolerance).
  • Eval 2: Guardrail panel replacement, post extraction, and hardware torquing audit.
  • Eval 3: High-speed debris extraction exercise executed safely within 45 seconds.

title: Traffic Control & Script Management
content:
Effective traffic control requires a dual-layered approach: physical hardware placement to guide human drivers, and digital node manipulation to govern Local traffic behavior. SADOT personnel deploy traffic control measures during active lane closures, major crash recoveries, road maintenance, and total roadway detours to isolate work zones and prevent vehicle intrusion.

17.1 Operational Scope & Deployment Criteria
A. Physical Barrier Channelization Establishes a visual and physical barrier separating moving traffic from personnel, emergency responders, and state equipment during encroaching work.
B. Digital Traffic Node Manipulation Alters local road pathfinding logic for AI/Locals during moderate to major roadway closures, forcing automated traffic onto detour routes or stopping before work zones.
C. Manual Flagging Operations Uses STOP/SLOW paddles to safely alternate traffic direction through single-lane alternating operations, signal failures, or utility crossings. Stand on shoulders—never live lanes.
D. Advance Warning & Triangles Provides early visual warning during initial staging or disabled vehicle stops, compelling drivers to reduce speed and begin early lane transitions.
17.2 Field Execution, Script Controls, & Node Routing Protocols
Script Interface & Keybindings
/traffic : Open Traffic Control Script Menu
[E] : Place object / toggle node state
[X] : Confirm placement & exit mode
/flagman : Equip STOP/SLOW paddle
[Delete] : Stow paddle & exit flagman mode
Physical Hardware Spacing (The 5-Foot Rule)

Cones, pylons, flares, and barricades must be spaced at strict 5-foot intervals along tapers and buffers. Spacing objects greater than 5 feet apart creates game engine physics voids, allowing Local vehicles to punch directly through physical barricade lines into active work zones.

🔍 Inspect Intersection Grid Diagram (FIG 5.2)
FIG 5.2: Divided Highway Intersection Channelization Waypoint Node Matrix
Traffic Node Logic & Local Behavior Matrix
GREEN NODES (Active Path) Open primary paths. Local drivers navigate here REGARDLESS of physical barricades or cones placed on top of them.
RED NODES (Restricted Path) Closed paths. Civilian Locals avoid Red nodes. Exception: Off-road vehicles (4x4s, SUVs, dirt bikes) ignore Red nodes.
The Detour Continuity Rule

If an operator disables road nodes (Red/Off) without providing an active, valid detour path (Green nodes), Local pathfinding logic fails, causing drivers to ignore node shutdowns and drive straight through work zones.

Mandatory Node Restoration

Prior to retrieving physical gear, operators must re-open /traffic and toggle all modified nodes back to Green/Active. Leaving nodes disabled causes phantom traffic jams and erratic behavior.

17.3 Specialized Training & Practical Qualification Curriculum
Instructional Modules
  • Module TC-1: Commands, keybindings, 5-foot spacing rules, and triangle tapers.
  • Module TC-2: Node overlays, Green/Red mechanics, and off-road exceptions.
  • Module TC-3: Detour construction, manual flagging, and post-operation resets.
Practical Field Evaluations
  • Eval 1: Construct a 100-ft lane closure taper with strict 5-foot object spacing.
  • Eval 2: Configure intersection nodes, disable straight paths, and test Local re-routing.
  • Eval 3: Deploy triangle tapers, regulate traffic via /flagman, and execute full node resets.

title: Towing & Transport Operations
content:
Towing and transport operations represent a core logistical function of the San Andreas Department of Transportation. Deployed technicians are responsible for clearing disabled, abandoned, or damaged vehicles from public thoroughfares, executing heavy-duty commercial recoveries, and transporting state equipment to maintain open transit corridors.

Mandatory MFO Form Logging Directive Every single vehicle tow, transport, relocation, or recovery operation executed by SADOT personnel must be formally logged into the Master Field Operations (MFO) Form immediately upon scene completion or transport delivery. Executing any transport without submitting a corresponding MFO Form entry constitutes an administrative documentation violation subject to progressive disciplinary action.
18.1 Operational Scope & Deployment Criteria
A. Disabled Vehicle Recovery Stranded due to mechanical failure, empty fuel, electrical faults, or flat tires. Logged under Owner's Request / Roadside section of the MFO Form.
B. Accident & Collision Recovery Requested by LEO or Fire/EMS at multi-vehicle crashes or rollovers after evidence processing. Logged under Accident Recovery section of the MFO Form.
C. Heavy-Duty Commercial Towing Requires specialized heavy assets (kenworthwrecker, navistarrollback, w900) for semi-trucks or buses. Requires HVY certificate class selection on MFO Form.
D. Equipment & Machinery Transport Scheduled movement of industrial assets via lowboys/trailers (trlowboy, cartrailer1). Requires Trailer certificate class and prime mover/trailer ID logging.
E. Vehicle & Asset Relocation Shifting legally parked or non-incident vehicles away from construction zones or parade routes without impounding. Logged under Relocation Log.
F. Impound & Abandoned Removal Official LEO requests for forensic holds or abandoned vehicles left past statutory time limits. Logged under LEO/Regular Impound with badge metrics and sign-off.
18.2 Field Execution & Recovery Protocols
Step 1: Staging & Pre-Hookup Safety Verification Position tow asset 10–15 ft ahead of target with arrow boards active. Cabin Verification (Life-Safety Mandate): Visually inspect interior to confirm zero occupants or animals remain inside before winching.
Step 2: Light/Medium Rollback Execution Workflow Tilt flatbed flush, attach J-hooks/bridle straps directly to factory tow hooks or solid frame points (never steering linkages or bumpers), winch vehicle on, press [E] for wheel tie-downs, and level bed.
Step 3: Heavy Wrecker & Uprighting Protocols Deploy hydraulic outriggers fully on solid pavement/cribbing. Rig dual snatch blocks around structural pillars for controlled rollover uprighting. Position wheel-lift under drive wheels, secure L-arms, pin locks, auxiliary tail lights, and secondary safety chains.
Step 4: Equipment Trailer Loading & Script Attachment (/attach) For lowboys (trlowboy), uncouple prime mover, toggle Extra 1 OFF and Extra 3 ON to drop ramps. Execute /attach in chat, select deck as base, target item, and use Numpad controls (8/5, 4/6, PageUp/Down, 7/9) to align flush. Lock with Numpad Enter.
Step 5: Mandatory MFO Form Documentation & Client Sign-Off Open MFO Form on onboard tablet. Input callsign, plate, make, model, color, pickup coordinates, destination yard, and certificate used. Obtain electronic signature on Section 14 before departing.
18.3 Specialized Training & Practical Qualification Curriculum
Instructional Modules
  • Module T-1: Rollback mechanics, winch angle math, frame rigging, and cabin checks.
  • Module T-2: Heavy wrecker outriggers, boom limits, rollover physics, and rigging.
  • Module T-3: Lowboy neck operations, /attach fine-tuning, and MFO Form filing.
Practical Field Evaluations
  • Eval 1: Rollback loading, cabin verification, [E] tie-downs, and MFO submission within 10 mins.
  • Eval 2: Lowboy disconnect, equipment loading, /attach alignment, and form logging.
  • Eval 3: Kenworth wrecker deployment, dual-cable rollover uprighting, wheel-lift, and LEO waiver.

title: Heavy Equipment Operation
content:
Operating industrial heavy machinery represents the highest tier of logistical capability within the San Andreas Department of Transportation. Heavy equipment is deployed for large-scale infrastructure repairs, macro-debris clearances, earthmoving operations, and bulk material handling where standard utility vehicles lack the hydraulic power or load capacity to execute the task.

Heavy Equipment Authorization Directive Operating heavy machinery including Bulldozers, Dump Trucks, Forklifts, and Heavy Lowboy Transport combinations is strictly restricted to personnel holding a verified Heavy Duty (HVY) Certification or Supervisory rank. Uncertified operation of heavy machinery is a major violation.
19.1 Operational Scope & Deployment Criteria
A. Dump Truck Operations High-volume asphalt hauling, storm debris extraction, gravel distribution, landslide removal, and staging as a crash-attenuation shadow vehicle.
B. Heavy Machinery & Bulldozers Structural collapses, mudslides, off-road hazard clearing, highway embankment reconstruction, or heavy barrier positioning using tracked propulsion.
C. Industrial Forklift Handling Precise vertical lifting, stacking, and offloading of palletized materials, crash cushions, sign structures, and cargo containers from lowboys.
D. Lowboy & Heavy Trailers Safe transport of tracked machinery across public roadways between maintenance compounds and work sites on multi-axle low-deck trailers (trlowboy).
19.2 Field Execution & Safety Protocols
Step 1: Pre-Operational Circle Check & Spotter Requirement Inspect hydraulic lines, fluid levels, track tension, coupling pins, and backup alarms. Ground Spotter Mandate: Operators must utilize a dedicated ground technician with high-vis gear and radio link when maneuvering near blind spots or overhead powerlines.
Step 2: Dump Truck Deployment & Unloading Protocol Park on firm, level ground. Clear area behind tailgate, unlatch locks, engage PTO lever, and raise bed gradually. For aggregate distribution, set tailgate safety chains to desired gap width and pull forward at constant low speed.
Step 3: Bulldozer & Earthmoving Operations Travel at low speeds with blades carried low (12 to 18 inches above ground). Keep blades flush during grading; avoid turning sharply on open asphalt without rubber matting to prevent track damage.
Step 4: Industrial Forklift Handling & Loading Verify cargo weight against rated capacity, spread tines wide, insert fully, tilt mast back slightly, and elevate cargo 4 to 6 inches above ground. Operate in reverse if forward sightlines are blocked.
Step 5: Lowboy Machinery Loading & MFO Logging Drop lowboy neck ramps (Extra 1 OFF, Extra 3 ON), drive bulldozer onto deck, secure with four independent Grade-70 transport chains and ratchet binders, and log prime mover/trailer metrics on the MFO Form.
19.3 Specialized Training & Practical Qualification Curriculum
Instructional Modules
  • Module HE-1: PTO mechanics, hydraulic limits, stability, and blind-spot management.
  • Module HE-2: Blade angling, track tensioning, earthmoving, and spotter hand signals.
  • Module HE-3: Mast controls, fork spacing, lowboy ramps, and chain binding math.
Practical Field Evaluations
  • Eval 1: Dump truck inspection, level staging, chain limits, and material spread simulation.
  • Eval 2: Bulldozer unloading, spotter coordination, debris push, and safe blade drop.
  • Eval 3: Forklift cargo staging, lowboy loading, four-point chain binding, and MFO submission.

title: Roadside Assistance Operations
content:
Roadside assistance operations are designed to rapidly resolve minor mechanical vehicle failures, assist stranded motorists, and clear live travel lanes without requiring full vehicle towing or transport. Deployed technicians act as a frontline safety utility, mitigating highway hazards and restoring transit throughput across state corridors.

Mandatory MFO Roadside Logging Directive All roadside assistance actions including tire changes, fuel deliveries, battery jumpstarts, lockout bypasses, and on-scene repairs must be immediately recorded within Section 13 (Roadside Service) of the Master Field Operations (MFO) Form prior to clearing coordinates.
20.1 Operational Scope & Deployment Criteria
A. Stranded Motorist Assistance Dispatched or flagged down for non-collision mechanical failures on shoulders, medians, or travel lanes. Shields motorist and provides immediate self-evacuation remedies. Logged under Section 13 on MFO.
B. Pneumatic Tire Modifications Vehicles immobilized by flat, blown, or compromised tires. Performs tool-compliant wheel exchanges or puncture plugs. Requires logging size class (Small, Medium, Large, Heavy HD) and tire count.
C. Emergency Fuel Replenishment Completely out-of-fuel vehicles on high-speed shoulders. Delivers limited emergency allocations (1 to 2 gallons) to enable self-evacuation to a fueling station. Logged with exact gallons.
D. Battery Jumpstarts & Recovery Dispatched for dead batteries, faulty starters, or drained systems. Utilizes auxiliary cable systems or heavy portable jump packs to re-initialize ignition. Logged as Battery Jumpstart.
E. Minor Repairs & Lockouts Cooling hose detachments, loose terminals, sensor faults, or door lockouts. Executes basic non-invasive adjustments or uses lockout kits. Logged as Lockout Service or On-Scene Mechanical Repair.
F. Rapid Lane Clearance (Push-Offs) Non-running vehicles in active high-speed lanes where flatbed rigging poses life-safety risks. Uses heavy utility push-bumpers (civtahoe, civramdot1, civf250) to displace vehicles onto shoulders.
20.2 Field Execution & Assistance Workflows
Step 1: Defensive Staging & Shadow Block Setup Position utility truck 25 to 50 ft behind disabled vehicle, angled toward the shoulder. Activate low-profile amber strobes, rear arrow boards, and deploy a 5-foot tapered line of traffic triangles if encroaching on live lanes.
Step 2: Pneumatic Tire Change & Wheel Exchange Workflow Park on level ground, set emergency brake, and place wheel chocks. Use hydraulic floor jacks at factory frame points, loosen lug nuts with an impact wrench, swap tire, hand-tighten in star pattern, lower jack, and torque to specification.
Step 3: Emergency Fuel Dispensation Protocol Confirm fuel type (Gasoline vs. Diesel). Maintain a 15-foot safety perimeter free of open flames or running engines. Dispense 1 to 2 gallons from approved safety cans and record exact gallons on MFO Form.
Step 4: Battery Jumpstart Protocol Connect red (+) to dead battery positive, then source positive. Connect black (-) to source negative, and ground remaining black (-) to an unpainted metal frame point on target vehicle. Idle state vehicle for 2–3 minutes before ignition attempt. Disconnect in exact reverse order.
Step 5: Controlled Vehicle Push-Off Execution Align heavy rubber push-bumper against target rear bumper. Brief driver to unlock steering wheel, shift into Neutral, and hold steering. Apply gentle forward throttle, pushing at under 5 mph until clearing live lanes.
Step 6: Mandatory MFO Form Logging & Sign-Off Open Section 13 of MFO Form on terminal. Input operator callsign, location, vehicle details, service type, tire scale class, and consumables used. Obtain motorist electronic signature on Section 14 (Waiver).
20.3 Specialized Training & Practical Qualification Curriculum
Instructional Modules
  • Module RA-1: Defensive staging, warning triangles, and motorist de-escalation.
  • Module RA-2: Jacking safety, torque patterns, fuel safety, and electrical polarity.
  • Module RA-3: Push-bumper alignment, low-speed physics control, and MFO logging.
Practical Field Evaluations
  • Eval 1: Staging, wheel chocks, tire exchange with star-pattern torque, and MFO entry.
  • Eval 2: Fuel type verification, emergency fuel dispensation, and polarity-safe jumpstarts.
  • Eval 3: Live-lane push-off exercise under 5 mph onto shoulder buffer with MFO log.

title: Emergency Response Operations
content:
SADOT units respond to active infrastructure crises, major multi-vehicle pile-ups, and natural roadway collapses. Apparatus responses must be conducted with due regard for public safety according to established dispatch priority codes.

Code 1 — Routine Response Pothole patching, sign re-erection, non-blocking curb remediation, and scheduled maintenance runs.
Posted Speed | Strobes OFF
Code 2 — Urgent Transit Shoulder vehicle disablements, debris encroaching on active highway lanes, and traffic signal outages.
+10 MPH Max | Roof Beacons ON
Code 3 — Critical Emergency Downed high-voltage lines, interstate rollovers with full blockages, sinkholes, and structural bridge damage.
Due Regard | 360° Amber & Sirens
Mandatory MFO Emergency Logging Directive All emergency response deployments including major crash clearing, storm debris removal, hazardous material spills, and emergency closures must be formally registered in the Master Field Operations (MFO) Form. Logging must be finalized immediately upon clearing scene coordinates.
21.1 Operational Scope & Deployment Criteria
A. Major Crash & Pileup Response Positions heavy buffer vehicles to protect emergency personnel, deploys lighting, and extracts wreckage once forensic holds clear. Logged under Accident Recovery section of MFO Form.
B. Roadway Hazards & Obstructions Rapidly isolates displaced cargo, rockslides, or pavement buckles using advance warning hardware. Logged under Section 13 (Roadside Service) or Relocation Log.
C. Flooding & Severe Inundation Deploys high-water warning signage, establishes hard barricade closures across flooded corridors, and clears drainage structures. Logged under Relocation / Roadside Service notes.
D. Fallen Trees & Storm Debris Deploys chainsaw teams, loaders, and grapple attachments to cut, drag, and clear fallen timber off live travel lanes. Logged under Roadside Service on MFO Form.
E. Downed Infrastructure & Utilities Establishes an extended perimeter around compromised utility assets, prevents entry, and coordinates power isolation. Logged under Roadside Service / Relocation Log.
F. Chemical & Fuel Spill Containment Deploys granular absorbents, constructs containment berms, isolates zones, and assists Fire/EMS HazMat units. Logged under Accident Recovery / Roadside Service with consumable quantities.
G. Emergency Road Closures Locks down access points, configures detours, and modifies traffic nodes for active shooter events or major fires. Logged under Section 12 (Relocation / Scene Control).
21.2 Field Execution & Emergency Protocols
Step 1: Emergency Staging & Unified Command Handshake Stage vehicles 25 to 50 ft back from hazard boundary, angled at 45 degrees for a hard metal buffer. Report to LEO or Fire/EMS Scene Commander and operate under their direction until roadway control is officially transferred.
Step 2: Major Crash Isolation & Scene Illumination Deploy 5-foot spaced cone taper using /traffic. Position lighting arrays across extraction areas without blinding drivers. Clear glass/shards using heavy brooms and absorbents once forensic evidence is released.
Step 3: Storm Debris, Tree, & Flooding Operations Establish drop zone perimeters for chainsaws; drag timber onto shoulders. If flood depth exceeds 4 inches, deploy Type III barricades and VMS boards (ROAD CLOSED / FLOODING). Disable straight-through nodes via /traffic.
Step 4: Downed Power Lines & Infrastructure Isolation The 50-Foot Rule: Always treat overhead wires as live and lethal; maintain a minimum 50-foot standoff distance. Block all approaching lanes with heavy trucks and barricades. Never drive equipment over wires.
Step 5: Chemical & Fuel Spill Containment Identify HazMat placards from a safe upwind distance. Spread clay absorbent from the outer edge inward to protect storm drains. Fall back immediately for toxic/explosive cargo to let Fire/EMS HazMat handle primary mitigation.
Step 6: Emergency Detours & Post-Scene Node Restoration Deploy detour signage and configure Green node turn paths. Once cleared, re-open /traffic and toggle all modified nodes back to original Green/Active state. Submit MFO Form before marking 10-8.
21.3 Specialized Training & Practical Qualification Curriculum
Instructional Modules
  • Module ER-1: Unified Command, LEO/Fire interfacing, truck angling, and lighting.
  • Module ER-2: Chainsaw safety, tree rigging, flood thresholds, and detour node routing.
  • Module ER-3: Placard ID, spill absorption, 50-foot powerline rules, and MFO Form filing.
Practical Field Evaluations
  • Eval 1: Crash staging, 5-ft cone taper, light array placement, and MFO entry in 10 mins.
  • Eval 2: Barricades, Green node detour setup via /traffic, timber clearance, and node reset.
  • Eval 3: Fuel spill absorption ring, 50-ft powerline safety perimeter, and MFO form audit.

title: Infrastructure Maintenance
content:
Infrastructure maintenance encompasses the long-term upkeep, structural restoration, and safety compliance of fixed state transit assets. SADOT infrastructure crews maintain structural barriers, drainage channels, bridge decks, pavement markings, and highway lighting arrays to guarantee long-term system stability and prevent catastrophic environmental or mechanical road failures.

Mandatory MFO Infrastructure Logging Directive All infrastructure repairs, structural inspections, drainage clearing, and streetlight servicing must be formally logged within the Master Field Operations (MFO) Form immediately upon completion of site operations.
22.1 Operational Scope & Deployment Criteria
A. Guardrail & Barrier Systems Repairs compromised steel W-beams, tension cables, or displaced concrete Jersey barriers to prevent vehicles from leaving the road or crossing medians. Logged under Relocation / Roadside Service.
B. Perimeter Fencing & Security Maintains physical barriers along right-of-way fencing to prevent livestock, wildlife, or unauthorized pedestrians from wandering onto high-speed travel lanes. Logged under Roadside Service / Infrastructure notes.
C. Bridge & Expansion Joints Preserves bridge structural integrity, seals expansion joints against water intrusion, and repairs deck spalling or potholes. Logged under Relocation / Infrastructure Log.
D. Drainage Systems & Culverts Clears catch basins, silted culverts, and ditches to direct stormwater runoff away from pavement sub-bases, preventing hydroplaning and washouts. Logged under Roadside Service.
E. Road Markings & Delineation Applies high-visibility thermoplastic striping and reflective pavement markers (RPMs) to guide motorists and maintain lane discipline day and night. Logged under Roadside Service.
F. Streetlights & Lighting Arrays Restores overhead illumination at key interchanges, pedestrian crossings, and high-risk corridors to optimize nighttime driver sightlines. Logged under Roadside Service.
Field Execution & Safety Protocols
Step 1: Work Zone Protection & Shadow Staging Deploy arrow trucks (civf550dot or civramdot2) 250 to 500 feet upstream with a 5-foot spaced cone taper using /traffic.
Step 2: Guardrail, Barrier, & Fence Repair Workflow Unbolt crushed W-beams, drive new steel I-beam posts, mount replacement panels overlapping in traffic direction. Realign concrete Jersey barriers using a heavy wrecker (kenworthwrecker) or loader. Tension chain-link fabric across line posts.
Step 3: Bridge Deck & Expansion Joint Maintenance Clear debris from expansion joints using compressed air/washers. Inject elastomeric polymer sealants and apply rapid-setting high-strength concrete patch material to spalled deck areas.
Step 4: Culvert & Drainage Clearing Protocol De-silt culvert inlets/outlets using hydro-vacuum equipment or manual shovels. Lay heavy rip-rap stone around headwalls and ditches to slow water velocity.
Step 5: Roadway Marking & Striping Application Sweep pavement clean. Apply heated thermoplastic compound at specified line widths (4-inch edge lines, 10-foot dashed lanes), dropping retroreflective glass beads directly onto hot paint.
Step 6: Streetlight Maintenance & Bucket Truck Safety Position aerial bucket truck on level ground, extend outriggers, tether safety harnesses, isolate electrical feeds, replace LED/HPS luminaire heads or photocells, and lower basket safely.
Step 7: Post-Maintenance Cleanup & MFO Logging Clear all scrap metal, concrete debris, paint cans, and hand tools. Complete and submit the Master Field Operations (MFO) Form prior to departing scene coordinates.
22.3 Specialized Training & Practical Qualification Curriculum
Instructional Modules
  • Module IM-1: Guardrail tension specs, W-beam torque limits, and fence standards.
  • Module IM-2: Expansion joint dynamics, concrete patching, culvert flow, and erosion.
  • Module IM-3: Thermoplastic glass bead application, bucket truck safety, and MFO filing.
Practical Field Evaluations
  • Eval 1: Work zone staging, W-beam replacement, barrier alignment, and MFO logging.
  • Eval 2: Culvert de-silting, erosion stone placement, and thermoplastic striping audit.
  • Eval 3: Bucket truck positioning, luminaire head swap, bridge joint seal injection, and cleanup.

title: Snow & Severe Weather Operations
content:
Severe weather events including winter freezing, blizzards, torrential downpours, flash flooding, and high-wind severe storms dramatically compromise roadway traction, obscure visual sightlines, and threaten public infrastructure. SADOT winter and severe weather teams deploy specialized equipment and anti-icing tactics to maintain open transit corridors, prevent cold-weather pileups, and restore safe travel conditions across the state.

Mandatory MFO Weather Logging Directive All winter and severe weather deployments including snowplowing, chemical spreading, storm debris removal, flood closures, and emergency barricade setups must be formally logged into the Master Field Operations (MFO) Form immediately upon concluding shift operations.
23.1 Operational Scope & Deployment Criteria
A. Storm Debris & Windfall Clearance Rapidly sweeps and extracts windblown hazards from high winds or microbursts to prevent collisions. Logged under Section 13 (Roadside Service) on MFO Form.
B. Severe Flood & High-Water Response Positions high-water warning signage, establishes closures across submerged sectors, and clears catch basins. Logged under Relocation / Roadside Service notes.
C. Ice Control & Snow Removal Deploys snowplow blades, liquid anti-icing brines, and granular salt/sand spreaders to melt ice and clear snow down to bare pavement. Logged under Roadside Service with material quantities.
D. Storm Damage Restoration Executes priority temporary stabilization and structural repairs for wind-damaged signage, guardrails, or washed-out shoulders. Logged under Relocation / Infrastructure Log.
E. Emergency Weather Barricades & Closures Establishes hard barricades, activates VMS boards, and modifies traffic nodes during blizzards or severe flooding where travel threatens human life. Logged under Section 12 (Relocation / Scene Control).
23.2 Field Execution & Weather Response Protocols
Step 1: Pre-Departure Fleet Verification & Cold-Weather Staging Inspect tire treads, fluid levels, wipers, strobes, and defrosters. Fill hoppers with salt/sand or liquid brine; verify utility boxes contain flares, cold-weather PPE, high-vis gear, and tow straps.
Step 2: Snowplowing & Anti-Icing Spreading Execution Pre-treat bridge decks and shaded curves with liquid brine. Operate plows in an echelon (staggered tandem) formation on multi-lane highways. Maintain a maximum operating speed of 25 to 30 mph during plowing.
Step 3: Storm Debris & Windfall Extraction Stage utility trucks 25 to 50 ft upstream with amber strobes active. Use chainsaws to buck fallen timber and tow straps/loaders to drag logs into the shoulder clear zone.
Step 4: Severe Weather Barricade Placement & Node Routing Deploy Type III hard barricades across travel lanes at 5-foot spacing intervals using /traffic. Position VMS trailer displaying ROAD CLOSED / SEVERE WEATHER and disable straight-through nodes.
Step 5: Post-Storm Recovery & MFO Form Documentation Re-open /traffic and toggle all modified nodes back to original Green/Active state. Submit MFO Form documenting hours plowed, miles treated, and salt/brine tonnage consumed.
23.3 Specialized Training & Practical Qualification Curriculum
Instructional Modules
  • Module W-1: Anti-icing chemistry, brine application, and freeze-point mechanics.
  • Module W-2: Snowplow blade adjustments, tandem echelon geometry, and wing-plows.
  • Module W-3: Storm closures, emergency barricades, VMS messaging, and MFO logging.
Practical Field Evaluations
  • Eval 1: Pre-trip inspection, spreader calibration, 25 mph plowing pass, and MFO log.
  • Eval 2: Defensive staging, advance warning deployment, and windfall clearance audit.
  • Eval 3: 5-foot interval barricade placement, VMS setup, node re-routing, and full node reset.

title: Work Zone Setup & Temporary Traffic Control
content:
Work zone setup and Temporary Traffic Control (TTC) establish the foundational safety architecture for all state infrastructure maintenance, roadway repairs, emergency responses, and commercial recovery operations. SADOT operators utilize standardized geometric layouts and physical channelization to construct impenetrable safety corridors.

Mandatory MFO Work Zone Logging Directive ALL work zone setups, temporary lane closures, detour configurations, and construction lighting deployments must be formally registered in the Master Field Operations (MFO) Form under Section 3 (Flag & Traffic Log) or Section 12 (Relocation / Scene Control) prior to clearing coordinates.
24.1 Operational Scope & Deployment Criteria
A. Cones & Channelizers Mandatory for all active lane closures. Forms continuous visual lines guiding traffic away from hazards.
B. Hard Buffer Barriers Type I, II, or III barricades used for total shutdowns or long-term construction to physically block vehicle entry.
C. Arrow Boards Required on all mobile utility trucks (civf550dot). Compels approaching motorists to execute early lane changes.
D. Variable Message Boards (VMS) Positioned 500-1,000ft upstream. Provides custom text advisories regarding upcoming merges or detours.
E. Temporary Traffic Lights Deployed for single-lane alternating traffic on two-lane roads, replacing manual flaggers for long durations.
F. Detour Signage Established along alternate routes during total corridor shutdowns to ensure legally compliant navigation.
24.2 Field Execution & Setup Protocols
Step 1: Pre-Setup Layout Planning Calculate taper distances based on speed. City (5-10ft intervals) vs Highway (10-20ft intervals). Observe the 5-Foot Spacing Rule for physical barricades to prevent physics voids.
Step 2: Sequential Deployment Deploy in a strict downstream sequence: Advance warning staging → VMS placement → Taper construction → Work area buffer.
Step 3: Script Control (/traffic) Disable straight-through nodes (Red) and ensure turning nodes (Green) are active for detours. Restore nodes to Green/Active before retrieving hardware.
24.3 Training & Practical Qualification
Modules WZ-1 to WZ-3
  • MUTCD Geometry & Spacing.
  • Script Integration & Node Logic.
  • Lighting & Site Restoration.
Practical Evaluations
  • 100ft High-Speed Taper setup.
  • Intersection Detour configuration.
  • Night lighting & Node reset audit.

content:

Through unified tactical execution, meticulous geometric safety corridors, and absolute communication discipline, SADOT keeps the state moving forward safely with integrity.
